programme.desc: In 1983, the quiet English village of Narborough was shattered by the brutal rape and murder of 15-year-old Lynda Mann. Three years later, a second teenager, Dawn Ashworth, was found dead in eerily similar circumstances. Relatives and friends of Lynda and Dawn paint a picture of the lost innocence and the terror that gripped a small town. Detectives involved in the original investigation recount the painstaking work that led to an unprecedented scientific breakthrough. For the first time ever, DNA profiling was used to eliminate a suspect-and eventually identify the true perpetrator: Colin Pitchfork. Through archive footage and firsthand accounts, this documentary unravels how one of the most groundbreaking forensic investigations in history brought a serial killer to justice-and forever changed criminal investigations worldwide. Exec Prod Andy Dunn/Daniel Smith; Prod/Dir: Sam Budd; ITN

programme.desc: Britain was told Lucy Letby was a killer. But what if the evidence tells a different story? A shocking new investigation by The Sun, in partnership with 5, puts the prosecution's case under the microscope like never before. Shocking, fresh revelations uncover a hospital in crisis and a system in freefall... and asks the toughest of all questions: were those institutional failures misinterpreted as cold-blooded murder? Through new testimony, expert analysis and an anonymous insider, investigative journalist Rob Pattinson examines whether important alternative explanations were overlooked during the investigation. The film explores the possibility that the focus on one individual may have obscured wider problems within the hospital. Could Letby have been nothing more than a scapegoat for systemic failures inside the unit? Lucy Letby: the nation's worst serial killer... or one of the biggest scapegoats in British history? programme.desc: Play for Today returns with six original films that continue the strand's commitment to championing emerging talent both on and off screen. Daniel Mays, Joel Fry and Amit Shah star in a survival dramedy set in the breathtaking yet unforgiving Scottish Highlands. Lou (Mays), Dev (Shah), and Alistair (Fry), three old friends clinging to their annual wild camping tradition, begin their trip with banter, nostalgia, and amateur vlogging, but soon unravel into a battle of egos, secrets, and survival when they get lost, food runs short, and friendships fracture. At once funny, poignant, and unsettling, Wild explores the line between adventure and recklessness, and how toxic masculinity has become a huge part of the epidemic decline in men's mental health. Writer: Lewis Wren; Dir: BRICK; Vertigo Films
